images.title: Area with decimal sides
images.purpose: Show that the area of a rectangle with decimal sides is still length times breadth, found through fractions.
images.composition: One wide rectangle sits in the centre with its two side lengths marked outside it and two short lines of working inside it; white space around.
exact_structure: One rectangle, wider than tall (width to height about 7 to 3), filled light teal #0072B2 with a #2B2B2B outline, centred.
Along the bottom edge, an amber #E69F00 dimension line with the label "13.3 cm".
Along the left edge, an amber #E69F00 dimension line with the label "5.7 cm".
Inside the rectangle, two centred lines of dark text #1F2937: "57/10 × 133/10 = 7581/100" on the first line and "Area = 75.81 sq cm" on the second, the second line in reddish purple #CC79A7.
No grid lines inside the rectangle, no other shapes or numbers.
rejection: the side lengths swapped onto the wrong edges or written as other numbers
any area other than 75.81 sq cm or any numerator other than 7581
a grid or squares drawn inside the rectangle
images.takeaway: Area = length × breadth works for decimal sides: 5.7 × 13.3 = 75.81 sq cm.
images.description: A teal rectangle with sides 13.3 cm and 5.7 cm, holding the working 57/10 × 133/10 = 7581/100 and Area = 75.81 sq cm.
images.context: Shown beside the rectangle worked example in the concept on walking distance and area.
images.teaching_notes: Read the two sides, write each as tenths, and see why the area comes out in hundredths.

image_decisions.why: A labelled rectangle carries the area example directly and keeps the decimal working tied to the shape.
